patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents requesting prenatal care, reporting 2 months of increasing breast tenderness, nausea, a 6.6 lb weight gain, increased urinary frequency, and uncertainty about the date of her last menstrual period. She stopped taking oral contraceptives 6 months ago and has been trying to conceive with her husband since then. She believes she is pregnant and was happy to share this news with her husband last week.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Stopped oral contraceptives 6 months prior in an attempt to conceive.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Reports being in a stable relationship and actively trying to conceive with her husband.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or flank pain.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with symptoms suggestive of early pregnancy.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“I think I’m pregnant and I wanted to start prenatal care. For about two months I’ve had increasing breast tenderness, nausea, and a 6.6 lb weight gain, plus I’ve been urinating more often.”
When was the first day of your last menstrual period (LMP), and has it been regular?

“I’m not exactly sure of the first day of my last menstrual period, and my cycles haven’t been very predictable since I stopped my oral contraceptives. I’ve been trying to conceive with my husband for the past several months, and I’ve felt these symptoms for about two months.”
Have you taken a home pregnancy test, and if so, what was the result?
“Yes, I took a home pregnancy test a few days ago, and it was positive.”
Do you have any abdominal or pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, or dizziness?
“No, I don’t have any abdominal or pelvic pain, and I haven’t had vaginal bleeding or dizziness.”
How many times have you been pregnant before, including any miscarriages or abortions, and how many children do you have?
“I’ve never been pregnant before—I’ve had no miscarriages or abortions, and I don’t have any children yet.”
Have you ever had pelvic inflammatory disease, sexually transmitted infections like chlamydia or gonorrhea, or any surgery on your fallopian tubes or ovaries?
“No, I’ve never had pelvic inflammatory disease, and I don’t have a history of chlamydia or gonorrhea. I’ve never had any surgery on my fallopian tubes or ovaries.”
Are you vomiting, and if so, how many times per day, and are you able to keep fluids down?
“I haven’t been vomiting—just nausea. I’m able to keep fluids down and I haven’t had any trouble staying hydrated.”
Have you used any fertility medications or undergone fertility treatments such as IVF to conceive?
“I haven’t used any fertility medications or undergone IVF or other fertility treatments—I’ve just been trying naturally with my husband since I stopped my oral contraceptives.”
Have you had a medical confirmation of the pregnancy with a blood test or ultrasound, and if so, what did it show?
“I haven’t had any blood test or ultrasound yet—only the positive home pregnancy test a few days ago. I came in today because I’m hoping to confirm it and start prenatal care.”
Have you noticed any milky discharge from your nipples, severe headaches, or vision changes?
“No milky discharge from my nipples. I haven’t had severe headaches or any vision changes.”
Do you have any burning, pain, or urgency when you urinate, or have you had any fever?
“No, I don’t have burning, pain, or urgency when I urinate, and I don’t have any fever.”
Do you smoke cigarettes or use any other tobacco products?
“I don’t smoke cigarettes or use any tobacco products.”
Do you have any chronic medical conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, or epilepsy?
“No, I don’t have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, or epilepsy. I’m generally healthy and haven’t been diagnosed with anything long-term.”
